faq: What kinds of images can it read?

Product photos, screenshots, receipts and scans are fine as long as they are clear. It describes and tags what it sees. It is not suited to medical, legal or identity decisions, and we do not build face recognition.
On clear content it is usually good, but never perfect. We test against samples you have labelled yourself, report how many it got right and flag uncertain items for a person to check.
We use providers whose business terms say your data is not used to train their models, and we process only the files you share. Share only what you are allowed to, and avoid sensitive personal data.
Can I use it on customer reviews?
Yes, to find themes and complaints in reviews you already have. We do not use it to write or alter reviews, and we do not scrape data from sites that forbid it.

desc:
Text and image analysis automation turns piles of reviews, emails, documents and product photos into tags, topics and summaries you can act on. Ecom Swift LLC builds the workflow, tunes it on your own samples and delivers results in a spreadsheet or your tools.

## What is text and image analysis automation?

It is a workflow that reads each item in a batch and writes down what it finds. For text, that might be the topic of an email, the sentiment of a review or a two-line summary of a long report. For images, it might be the product type, color or visible defects shown in a photo.

Each result is stored beside the original item, so you can sort, filter and count. The reading is done by an AI model, but the value comes from the rules around it: your categories, your examples and your definition of a correct label.

## Why manual sorting does not scale

Someone has to read the support inbox, scan the reviews and tag the photo library. When volume is small, that works. When it grows, the work becomes slow, uneven and easy to postpone, and patterns hide inside the pile. A complaint that appears forty times looks like forty separate problems.

Automation keeps the reading consistent. The same rule is applied to the first item and the thousandth, and the output is structured enough to count.

## How it improves results

Structured output lets you see what is actually happening. Counting complaint topics shows which product issue to fix first. Sorting emails by type routes them to the right person sooner. Tagging photos makes a catalog easier to filter and search.

Accuracy depends on your data and your categories. Clear definitions and good examples give better labels, and ambiguous items are bound to exist. That is why we flag edge cases for a person instead of forcing a guess.

## What a good analysis set-up includes

- A written definition of each task, such as which topics count as a billing complaint.
- Your own categories and labels, rather than a fixed list we choose.
- A tuning round on a sample batch, with results compared against your judgment.
- Clear handling of unclear items, which are flagged instead of guessed.
- Output in a spreadsheet with one row per item and a column for each label.
- A summary sheet with counts per category.
- Short accuracy notes explaining where the workflow is strong and where it is weak.
- Automatic runs on new items, where the source supports it.
- A regular digest email that summarizes what changed.
- A handover guide for editing categories later.

## What we do

You send a sample batch. We read it, draft the categories with you and run the workflow, then compare its labels with yours and adjust the instructions until the results look right. Only then do we run it on the full set.

The Basic package handles one task on a sample and a larger run. The Standard package covers two tasks with your categories, a summary sheet and flagged edge cases. The Premium package adds more tasks, runs on new items automatically, sends a digest and connects to your helpdesk or store. Your data is processed only for your project, and we tell you which provider reads it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Send a varied sample that includes messy, short and unusual items.
- Define each label in one clear sentence.
- Review the flagged edge cases and feed corrections back.
- Decide in advance what you will do with the results.
- Remove private details from the data where you can.

**Avoid:**
- Creating dozens of overlapping categories.
- Treating every label as certain without checking a sample.
- Running automatic actions, such as refunds, on unchecked labels.
- Sending sensitive images or records without agreeing how they are handled.
- Changing categories halfway through a run.

## Who it is for

A store owner with thousands of reviews wants to know which complaints repeat. A support lead needs incoming emails sorted by topic before the team starts the day. A catalog manager has product photos that need consistent tags for filtering.

## What we need from you

Send a sample batch, your preferred categories if you have them and a note on what you plan to do with the results. For a connected pipeline, we ask to join your helpdesk or store as a collaborator or staff user, or you can send exports. We never need passwords. After you order we send a short checklist and share the first results for your review.
